access.edition_or_version: Undelivered speech, self-published 15 May 1936; the dossier does not name a consulted edition

tone_mechanisms_observed: indictment catalog with parallel syntax: cumulative parallel clauses enumerate caste's effects before the refusal
negation/antithesis marking the boundary of what is refused
moral warrant: resistance argued from a stated principle, not from a mood
concrete named power and concrete stake: the Shastras and the caste order named rather than an abstraction; the stake is social emancipation
mechanics.emotional_progression: Cumulative indictment builds pressure toward an explicit refusal (dossier section D).
mechanics.warrant_note: Caste and religious authority are the warrant: caste subordinates ethical and public life, so its foundation must be destroyed for emancipation (dossier section E).
mechanics.language_note: English-language Indian text: the warrant is Indian even where the language is not, an explicit limit on any 'non-Anglophone' claim (dossier section E).
mechanics.verification_note: Undelivered speech, refused by the Jat-Pat Todak Mandal and self-published 15 May 1936; verified via publisher/archive records; no text reproduced (dossier section F).
